subject: Request: temporary pilot burst lane for Aquila Labs – dedicated GPU buffer
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary pilot burst lane for Aquila Labs – dedicated GPU buffer

Team —

We have a time-boxed pilot with Aquila Labs next week (week of 6/28). They want a short high-throughput run for model evaluation: roughly 48–72 hours of sustained load peaking at ~120 requests/min with average tokens per request ~3k. Sales has signaled this is important for conversion and the client is willing to cover incremental infra costs, but procurement needs a clear runbook and cost estimate.

Ask: can Infra make a temporary dedicated buffer ("pilot burst lane") that guarantees 4x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved for the window? If not full reservation, what is the minimum autoscale-override we can safely grant that meets SLOs and avoids cascading impact on other Dedicated customers?

Constraints / preferred approach:
- Start window: 2026-06-29 10:00 PT (approx) — end by 2026-07-02 10:00 PT (72h max).
- We need logs/audit for the window and a snapshot of latency/cost per token.
- If there's a meaningful risk to existing Dedicated SLAs, propose mitigations (e.g., move some lower-priority non-prod pools to staging).

Attached: pilot-run-sla.pdf (draft SOW), expected-load.csv (traffic profile).

Please reply with feasibility, required lead time, and any gating questions. If this requires an explicit exception to autoscaling policy, flag it here so I can escalate.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary pilot burst lane for Aquila Labs – dedicated GPU buffer

Laura —

Thanks for the heads up and the attachments. Short answer: probably doable but with caveats. A few quick clarifying Qs before I can commit to the exact shape of the exception:

1) Can you confirm whether the traffic is steady at ~120rpm or bursty spikes to that level? The difference drives whether sustained reservations are needed or whether we can rely on transient burst capacity.
2) Exact model variant and sequence lengths (we need peak sequence len to determine memory footprint).
3) Is the pilot tolerant of a few-minute throttle during the first 30 minutes of the window as caches/warmup complete?

Operational notes / options:
- Option A: carve out a 4-GPU temporary reservation from the non-prod buffer and flip it to the customer pool for the 72h window. This is lowest-risk but requires clearing the non-prod workloads first (24–36h lead).
- Option B: grant an autoscale override to allow Dedicated pools to exceed baseline caps by X GPUs for the window. This is faster but reduces headroom for failover and needs an explicit SLA exception.
- Option C: steering: route Aquila traffic to a lower-tier model variant with higher throughput (if acceptable) and avoid GPU reservation.

We’ll need a ticket in the Infra runbook for the override with exact times and a rollback plan. If we go Option B I’ll need an approval email chain that includes platform leads (Karthik) and a note about cost treatment (will Sales take the incremental bill?).

I can start prep work tomorrow but I’ll need the answers above.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2026 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary pilot burst lane for Aquila Labs – dedicated GPU buffer

Quick answers / context from Sales:

- Traffic profile: mostly steady for the ~48h window once started; there may be a 2–3 hour warmup ramp. Peak sustained ~120rpm as Laura noted; not frequent millisecond spikes.
- Model: open-llama-70b (quantized variant) with max seq len ~3k tokens.
- Customer is ok with short warmup throttling (first 15–30 min).
- Cost / billing: Aquila intends to reimburse incremental infra costs via a short procurement PO (procurement@aquila.ai). I’ve copied Simon (CTO) on a separate thread to confirm.

Sales preference: Option A if timing works (guaranteed performance for conversion). Option B is acceptable if the infra team prefers it, but Sales will need a firm SLA note for the customer and a cost estimate.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary pilot burst lane for Aquila Labs – dedicated GPU buffer

Thanks for the details — I’m granting a conditional exception (Option B with mitigations). Summary of decision and next steps: 

Decision: Approve autoscale override to allow +4 GPU headroom for the Aquila pilot window (2026-06-29 10:00 PT to 2026-07-02 10:00 PT) under the following conditions:
- Infra (Dev) implements a hard rollback at window end to avoid drift.
- We limit the override to the specific Dedicated pool tagged "pilot-aquila-2026"; no cross-pool borrow.
- Platform monitoring alert rules will be temporarily tightened (latency 95th and GPU saturation). Service owner must ack alerts within 10 minutes during the window.
- Cost treatment: Sales to confirm whether Aquila reimburses or we absorb for ARR-led pipeline. If reimbursed, Procurement and Finance need the DocuSign and PO before the window; otherwise we’ll run as marketing/sales expense.

Dev: please create the Infra runbook entry, the override ticket, and the rollback Playbook by EOD Wednesday (2026-06-23). Laura / Marissa: confirm the start time and secure the PO / DocuSign link. I’ll loop in CS on monitoring and NOC for the window.

If anything changes on model variant or expected tokens, escalate immediately.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
VP, Engineering Operations, Redwood Inference
